§9.1: импульс тела есть произведение его массы на скорость

§9.3: разошедшиеся суммы «до» и «после» опровергают сохранение импульса в этом процессе

texts.text:
<definition id="fs-id1165036767566">
<term>kinetic energy</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165038247619">energy of motion, one-half an object’s mass times the square of its speed</meaning>
</definition>

<note id="fs-id1165036884203">
<title>Work-Energy Theorem</title>
<para id="fs-id1165036972359">The net work done on a particle equals the change in the particle’s kinetic energy:</para>
<equation id="fs-id1165037940073"><m:math><m:mrow><m:msub><m:mi>W</m:mi><m:mrow><m:mtext>net</m:mtext></m:mrow></m:msub><m:mo>=</m:mo><m:msub><m:mi>K</m:mi><m:mi>B</m:mi></m:msub><m:mo>−</m:mo><m:msub><m:mi>K</m:mi><m:mi>A</m:mi></m:msub><m:mo>.</m:mo></m:mrow></m:math>
</equation>
</note>

<definition id="fs-id1165038306067">
<term>work-energy theorem</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165037270191">net work done on a particle is equal to the change in its kinetic energy</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1165038026773">
<term>average power</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165036771180">work done in a time interval divided by the time interval</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1165039295908">
<term>conservative force</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165035706005">force that does work independent of path</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1165039477062">
<term>non-conservative force</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165039052463">force that does work that depends on path</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1165038024912">
<term>energy conservation</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165037181302">total energy of an isolated system is constant</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1165038016114">
<term>mechanical energy</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165037047747">sum of the kinetic and potential energies</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1167133546182">
<term>momentum</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1167133532866">measure of the quantity of motion that an object has; it takes into account both how fast the object is moving, and its mass; specifically, it is the product of mass and velocity; it is a vector quantity</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1167134928870">
<term>closed system</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1167131586266">system for which the mass is constant and the net external force on the system is zero</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1167134540321">
<term>Law of Conservation of Momentum</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1167134540326">total momentum of a closed system cannot change</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1167131257470">
<term>system</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1167131586212">object or collection of objects whose motion is currently under investigation; however, your system is defined at the start of the problem, you must keep that definition for the entire problem</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1167134866786">
<term>elastic</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1167134570090">collision that conserves kinetic energy</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1167131552107">
<term>inelastic</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1167134942503">collision that does not conserve kinetic energy</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1167131501190">
<term>perfectly inelastic</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1167134507564">collision after which all objects are stuck together, moving with the same velocity; momentum is conserved, and the loss of kinetic energy is a maximum</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1167131501190">
<term>perfectly inelastic</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1167134507564">collision after which all objects are motionless, the final kinetic energy is zero, and the loss of kinetic energy is a maximum</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1165039354076">
<term>work</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165035663968">done when a force acts on something that undergoes a displacement from one position to another</meaning>
</definition>

§9.3: результирующая внешняя сила, действующая на систему в течение процесса
